S87.01.needs: an owner or admin account on a Team or Enterprise workspace
S87.01.note: The plan name is in the posture data but the overview does not show it as a line; check Billing for the plan. The Settings opener from the main screen was not confirmed (the command palette has a Settings entry at packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:96).
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin of a Team or Enterprise workspace.
Open Settings, then the Workspace tab, then click Workspace administration.
The page opens on Overview. Read the workspace name shown as the large heading.
Read the line under it that gives the time of the live read and the count of items needing attention.
Scroll the signal cards: Identity, Provisioning, Access (Members, Pending invitations, Seats), AI controls, Data, Residency and keys, Audit, Usage and spend.
Compare with Expected: name, members/seats and security posture should match the live workspace.

S87.02.needs: an owner or admin account on a Team or Enterprise workspace
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin.
Open Settings > Workspace, then click Workspace administration.
Click Members in the left menu.
Find the card titled Members and read each row: the name, the email under it, and the role.
Compare with Expected: every workspace member should appear with name, email and role.

S87.03.needs: an owner or admin account, and a second account with the invited email address
S87.03.note: The invitee screen is at the invite page (apps/web/app/invite/page.tsx).
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Members, and find the Invite teammate card.
Type an email in Email address, pick a role in Role, then click Create invitation.
Check that a private invitation link appears and the seat count goes down.
Find Pending invitations. Click New link to renew one, or Revoke to cancel one, and confirm the dialog.
Open the invitation link as the invitee (the Accept invitation button) and check the invitee joins with the chosen role.
S87.03.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Invite teammate

S87.04.needs: an owner or admin account; a directory-synced group for the synced case
S87.04.note: Group creation and role saving are in WorkspaceRoles.tsx; the sync itself is run from the Identity page (Directory sync).
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles in Workspace administration.
Scroll to the Groups card and read each group name and its member count.
To create one, type a name in New group name and click Create group.
Tick roles for a group and click Save group.
Compare with Expected: groups show members, and roles on a group are saved. A synced group says it is managed by its source and is read-only for its name and members.
S87.04.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles > Groups

S87.05.needs: an owner or admin account and a second member account
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles.
Read the Roles card: each role and its permissions.
Read the Additional roles card to see which extra roles each member holds.
Go to Members, open a member's role select, choose another role, then click Change role in the confirm dialog.
Compare with Expected: the member's role changes. Then sign in as that member and check that the server now allows or refuses the matching actions.

S87.06.needs: an owner or admin account and a second member account
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Roles.
Click New role, type a name, tick permissions, then click Create role.
Click Edit on the role to change it, or Delete and confirm Delete role to remove it.
In Additional roles, tick the custom role for a member, then click Save roles.
Compare with Expected: the role appears with its permissions. Sign in as the member and check the permission takes effect.
S87.06.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles > New role

S87.07.needs: an owner or admin account on a paid Team or Enterprise workspace
S87.07.note: Change seats opens the public pricing page, which is outside the console.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Members.
In the Seats & billing card read Licensed, In use and Available.
Invite a member or remove one and see whether In use goes up or down.
Click Change seats (or Review contract for contract-priced workspaces) to see how seats are added.
Compare with Expected: the three numbers match the seats and members, and seats change as members come and go.
S87.07.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Seats & billing

S87.08.needs: the owner account and a second member account
S87.08.note: The exact condition that shows this card was not fully traced; it is rendered inside the Members page.
steps: Sign in as the current owner and open Members.
In the Workspace ownership card, choose a member in Member to receive ownership.
Click Transfer ownership, then read the Transfer ownership? dialog and confirm.
Read the Ownership transferred message that follows.
Compare with Expected: the new owner holds the owner role and the old owner gets the chosen role. Check the change from the other account.
S87.08.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Workspace ownership

S87.09.needs: an owner or admin account, a company domain they control, and access to its DNS
S87.09.note: The status label Domain verified is in the same file (line 40).
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Identity in Workspace administration.
In Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC), type a company domain in Email domain and click Add connection.
Copy the TXT record shown (Record type, Record name, Record value) and publish it in the domain's DNS.
Click Verify domain.
Compare with Expected: the status changes from Domain not verified to Domain verified, and only then is sign-in routed for that domain.
S87.09.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) > Email domain

S87.10.needs: an owner account, a verified domain, and a test SAML or OIDC identity provider
S87.10.note: Whether sign-in through the provider works is checked at sign-in, not on this console page.
steps: Sign in as the workspace owner, open Identity, and find Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC).
After the domain is verified, choose a Protocol: SAML 2.0 or OIDC.
Fill the provider fields (IdP metadata URL for SAML; OIDC discovery URL, client ID and client secret for OIDC), then click Add connection.
Check the connection appears with its provider type and domain.
Sign in as a member on that domain through the identity provider and check it works.
S87.10.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) > Add connection

S87.11.needs: an owner or admin account and a test identity provider that supports SCIM 2.0
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Identity, and find Directory sync (SCIM 2.0).
Under Connections, fill the form and click Add connection.
Under SCIM tokens, choose a Connection, type a Token name and click Mint token. Copy the token shown.
Set up the identity provider with the token; create, change and remove a test user there.
Compare with Expected: the member is created, updated and removed (deprovisioned) in the workspace, and Recent IdP activity lists the events.

S87.12.needs: an owner or admin account; an automation or test client that uses a key
S87.12.note: A service principal is created with the first workspace API key, so creating one goes through Create key.
steps: Open Identity and find the Service principals card; read each name, its permissions and its created date.
Click Disable on a principal, then confirm Disable principal. Check that the button now says Enable.
Open Audit, find Workspace API keys, and click Create key with scopes and an expiry (the No expiry option is there).
Click Revoke on a key and confirm Revoke key.
Compare with Expected: a disabled principal and a revoked key stop working for automations, and keys keep working after their creator leaves.
S87.12.where: Workspace administration > Identity > Service principals (disable); Workspace administration > Audit > Workspace API keys (keys)

S87.13.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
S87.13.note: The refusal message seen by a member was not traced in this pass; watch the chat when testing.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Models.
In Providers, click Block on a provider (or Approve on one to allow it).
In Models, use Filter models, click Approve or Block on a model, then click Save model policy.
Sign in as a member, open chat, and try to pick the blocked model.
Compare with Expected: the blocked model is refused; the page says Auto never reaches a blocked model.

S87.14.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
S87.14.note: The refusal is checked in the feature itself (chat, Code, desktop), not on this page.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
Find the Allow switches (for example Allow Skills or Allow Plugins) and turn one off.
Click Save features and defaults.
Under Exceptions, add an exception for a person or group and click Save exception if needed.
Compare with Expected: the switched-off feature is refused for members in the product (for example in chat or the desktop app).
S87.14.where: Workspace administration > Policy > Allow (feature) switches > Save features and defaults

S87.15.needs: an owner or admin account, a member account, and a connected connector
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
Under Catalog connectors, open a connector and set Read-only tools and Write tools to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
Click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and use that connector's read and write tools in chat.
Compare with Expected: an allowed tool runs, a tool set to Needs approval asks first, and a blocked tool is refused.

S87.16.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
Under Catalog connectors, click Block on a connector, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and look for that connector in the connectors list.
Try to connect it.
Compare with Expected: the blocked connector is not offered and cannot be connected. Repeat for Custom connectors (Allow custom connectors switch).
S87.16.where: Workspace administration > Connectors > Catalog connectors > Block

S87.17.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
S87.17.note: Per-item control exists for plugins only on this page; skills are switched as a whole on Policy.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Connectors.
In the Plugins card, type a plugin name and click Approve (or Block), then click Save policy.
Optionally, on Policy, turn the Skills or Plugins switch off and click Save features and defaults.
Sign in as a member and look at the plugins and skills they can install or use.
Compare with Expected: an approved plugin can be used, a blocked one cannot, and a switched-off feature is refused.

labels.text: Publish a plugin or a skill

S87.18.needs: an owner or admin account, a member account, and a plugin or skill .zip file
S87.18.note: Separation from the public directory was not checked in this pass.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Plugins.
In Publish a plugin or a skill, click Upload a plugin or skill and choose a plugin .zip (or a skill .zip with SKILL.md).
Wait for the scan to finish; accept any findings if asked, then check the plugin is listed in Workspace plugins.
Sign in as a member and look for the plugin under Plugins.
Compare with Expected: the member can browse and install the workspace's own plugin; Retire for everyone removes it.
S87.18.where: Workspace administration > Plugins > Publish a plugin or a skill

S87.19.needs: an owner or admin account, a shared project, and a member account
S87.19.note: The per-member access controls live in the project sharing component; how to open them from this console page was not fully traced.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Sharing.
Under Shared projects, read each shared project and who has access.
Open the project's sharing controls to see each member's access: Can view, Can edit or No access.
Click Stop sharing on a project and confirm it.
Compare with Expected: the project leaves Shared projects, and the members lose access to it.

S87.20.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
S87.20.note: No separate external-sharing switch was found; the Public sharing card is the closest control. Confirm the mapping with the owner.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Public sharing card, turn Allow public sharing off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to create a new public share link for a chat.
Compare with Expected: the share is refused and no new external link is created while the switch is off.

S87.21.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account with a chat or artifact
S87.21.note: This is the same card as S87.20.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Public sharing card, turn Allow public sharing off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to publish a chat or an artifact publicly.
Compare with Expected: publishing is refused while the switch is off.

S87.22.needs: an owner or admin account and a member account
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In the Memory card, turn Allow memory off, then click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and open Settings > Memory.
Compare with Expected: the member sees memory turned off and no memory is used in chats.

S87.23.needs: an owner or admin account and test conversations older than the window
S87.23.note: The Data page also has Retention by data type with its own Save button; the code sits on the Policy page for this item.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Policy.
In Retention window, set the days in Retention window in days.
Turn on Enforce the retention window (in the Enforce retention card) and confirm if asked.
Read the card text: chats idle for that many days are deleted each night, except under legal hold.
Check the Data page sweeps table (Retention by data type) after a run.
Compare with Expected: the setting is saved and the nightly sweep follows it. Deletion is permanent, so use only test data.

S87.24.needs: an Enterprise workspace (choosing a region needs an active Enterprise plan) and an owner or admin account
S87.24.note: Partly built: the audit says the EU region infrastructure is not yet set up and the owner decision is open, so an EU move may not complete.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Data.
In Data region, read the line Stored in <region>.
Choose a region in Move to, then click Request move and confirm.
Check the line that says a move was requested and that data stays in the current region until the move completes.
Compare with Expected: the request is recorded; a Cancel the move button is shown while it is pending.

S87.25.needs: an owner or admin account and a customer-managed key in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault
S87.25.note: Where this is offered (plan or region gating) was not traced; the page shows the server's refusal message when it is not offered.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, then click Data.
In Encryption key, choose a provider (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault), paste the key identifier and click Connect key.
Click Rotate and confirm Rotate key, then check Last rotated changes.
Click Revoke, enter a reason, then confirm Revoke key.
Compare with Expected: rotation and revocation are recorded and the status text changes; a refused state shows the server message instead of the controls.

S87.26.needs: an owner or admin account (the console is limited to owners and admins); a second network to test a refused sign-in
S87.26.note: The refusal rule runs on the server (apps/web/lib/ip-allow-list-gate.ts), so the screen only shows the list; how the first screen opens Settings was not traced.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin. Open Settings, then the Workspace pane, then click Workspace administration.
Under Controls, click Policy.

Scroll to the row IP allow list. Click the field Add an IP address or CIDR block, type a test range you can reach (for example 203.0.113.0/24) and press Enter. A range that leaves out your own address can lock you out.
Look at the text under IP allow list: it should say Members may only sign in to this workspace from one of these addresses or blocks.
Compare with Expected. A sign-in from an address outside the list should be refused, which needs a second network to check.
S87.26.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Controls > Policy, then the row IP allow list

S87.28.needs: an owner or admin account; some audit events already in the workspace
S87.28.note: No time-range filter was found in WorkspaceAuditSection.tsx, so the time-range part of Expected is not visible on this card.
steps: Open Records > Audit. Find the card titled Audit trail.
Open the All actions list and pick one action.
Open the Outcome and severity filters and pick a value in each.
Look at the table columns When, Actor, Action, Resource, Surface and Outcome. Only matching rows should stay and the count line should change.
Compare with Expected: filters should work on live data.
S87.28.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, then the card Audit trail

S87.29.needs: an owner or admin account; a browser that saves downloads
S87.29.note: The card text says exporting is recorded in the trail; whether the export event actually appears was not traced in code.
steps: Open Controls > Policy and find the row Audit export. Check that the switch Allow audit export is on.
Open Records > Audit. Set filters if you want a smaller export.
Click Export JSONL. The browser downloads a file.
Open the file. Each line should be one audit event.
Compare with Expected: the export should be recorded. Check the Audit trail for a new event. The SIEM streaming card on the same page needs an HTTPS endpoint to test.
S87.29.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, button Export JSONL (switch: Controls > Policy, row Audit export)

S87.30.needs: an owner or admin account; some Cloud usage in the chosen period
S87.30.note: The export is a daily CSV only; no export by model, provider or product area was found.
steps: Open Records > Usage. Click 7 days, 30 days or 90 days at the top to change the period.
Read the card Managed cloud usage: Credits used, Active members, Turns, Tokens in and Tokens out.
Scroll to the tables By member, By product area, By model and By provider. Check that each lists rows.
Click Export daily CSV and open the downloaded file.
Compare with Expected. The page says only settled Cloud usage is counted; Local and BYOK activity is not included.
S87.30.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Usage

S87.33.needs: an owner or admin account; managed usage near the cap to see a refusal
S87.33.note: Controls > Policy also has a row named Monthly spend cap (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx); how the two relate was not traced.
steps: Open Records > Usage and scroll to the bottom card Monthly spend limit.
Type a monthly amount in credits in the cap field and set the percent next to Alert at.
Pick a value in Spend limit enforcement (Off, Notify or Block) and read the line under it.
Click Set limit (or Update limit if a limit exists).
Compare with Expected: the limit should show against spend. With Block, a managed turn past the cap should be refused, which needs spend close to the cap to test.
S87.33.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Usage, then scroll to the card Monthly spend limit

S87.34.needs: an owner or admin account; a contract-priced plan to see the contract panel
S87.34.note: Expected says the console manages payment method, invoices and contract terms. The code shows a summary with a link to billing settings, plus WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx, whose visible text was not read.
steps: Open Records > Billing.
Read the card Plan and seats: the plan, the Seats used count and the seat note.
Read the card Manage billing. It says payment, invoices and plan changes are in billing settings. Click Billing settings to go there.
Compare with Expected. The page shows plan and seats, and a contract panel for contract-priced plans; payment, invoices and plan changes are not made on this page.
S87.34.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Billing

S87.36.needs: an owner or admin account; an existing legal hold
S87.36.note: Expected asks for a full workspace export of conversations, messages, files and artifacts. The only export found is HoldExportLink in WorkspaceDataControls.tsx; the file types it includes were not traced.
steps: Open Records > Data and find the card Legal holds.
Pick a hold in the list. If none exists, create one first with Place a hold (see S87.37).
Click Export records on that hold. The browser downloads the records held for it.
Open the file and check it holds conversations, messages, files or artifacts in a machine-readable format.
Compare with Expected. Export is offered per legal hold only; a whole-workspace export was not found.
S87.36.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Data, then the card Legal holds, then Export records on a hold row

S87.37.needs: an owner or admin account (placing and releasing is limited to owners and admins); a member account for the member scope
S87.37.note: The protection of held data from the sweep is enforced on the server; the screen shows only the sweep record.
steps: Open Records > Data and find the card Legal holds.
Click Place a hold. Pick a scope in Legal hold scope (whole workspace or one member), type a name and reason, then click Place hold.
Check that the new row shows Placed with a date and either Whole workspace or Member.
Click Release hold, read the confirmation, then choose Keep hold to cancel or Release hold to confirm.
Compare with Expected: a released hold shows Released. Look at the Retention sweeps card to check that held records were not deleted while the hold was active.
S87.37.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Data, then the card Legal holds

labels.text: No request, show the policy only

S87.39.needs: an owner or admin account; a member with at least one restriction to see a refusal
S87.39.note: The file writes the heading with the entity ’, which shows as a curly apostrophe.
steps: Open Controls > Policy and scroll past the policy sections to Explain a member’s policy.
Pick a member.
Pick a request in the request list, or keep No request, show the policy only. For a country check, type a two-letter code such as US in the country field.
Click Explain.
Compare with Expected. The result starts with Allowed. or Refused. and lists the allowed countries and surfaces, with the reason when refused.
S87.39.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Controls > Policy, then scroll to Explain a member’s policy

S87.40.needs: an owner or admin account; an integration to try the key (optional)
S87.40.note: Scope names come from the server list (grantableScopes) and are not written in this file. No documented API page was found, and the item was not checked against a live key.
steps: Open Records > Audit and scroll to Workspace API keys.
Type a name in the key name field, pick an expiry (30 days, 90 days, 1 year or No expiry), and tick at least one scope.
Click Create key. Copy the key shown under Copy the key now.
Find the key in the list. It shows its scopes, Last used and Expires.
Click Revoke, read the confirmation, and confirm. Compare with Expected: the key should show scopes and an expiry, and after Revoke it should show Revoked.
S87.40.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Records > Audit, then the card Workspace API keys
